issue: Automatic context compaction repeats after one or two tool batches

readOnlyDiagnosis.cause: The automatic trigger used serialized bytes divided by two even when provider input usage was available. Fitting immediately below that trigger left little space for the next tool batch.

changes: Persist the normal request's history/tool-size anchor and use reported input plus a 10 percent margin and conservatively estimated new material.
Count cached input as occupied context. Use the previous conservative estimate for unknown or stale measurements.
Invalidate anchors on summary, preview projection, clear, restore, rollback, model switch, or changes to memory/profile/image projection.

Before requesting a model summary, try reducing old model-only tool previews to 75 percent of the input allocation with meaningful space recovered. Preserve the latest complete batch and original operation cards.

Use model summaries when previews cannot create enough space. Summarize older complete turns even when fixed overhead prevents retaining a nominal 16 KB summary reserve; do not commit no-op automatic previews.
Keep the user's context/output budgets and existing execution permissions unchanged.
regressions: Fourteen real read-tool batches against a temporary log exceed the old byte trigger but produce no compaction when reported input remains below the allocation.
Measurement anchors survive reload and include subsequent assistant/tool content and tool-catalog growth.
Unknown, zero, stale-model and changed-projection measurements fall back conservatively.
Old output preview reduction preserves latest raw results, user messages, call pairing, full operation records and enough space for a subsequent small batch.
High reported input still triggers a summary when the byte estimate is smaller; fixed overhead must not turn this into no-op maintenance.
Existing forced summary, output-limit retry, failure preservation, SRE investigation and context counter regressions remain covered.
